top_choice_rationale: Targeted protein degradation is a new chemical design principle, induced proximity by designed bifunctional molecules that recruit E3 ligases, established by Crews and Deshaies and made a rational design discipline by Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex work. It is widely reproduced and lets researchers remove targets that inhibitors cannot reach. The missing approved degrader is a real maturity concern, but base editing (P001) carries a comparable one plus proximity to the 2020 CRISPR prize and the Target-AID attribution issue, so I keep P002 first. The citation must stay on bifunctional degraders and not claim the cereblon molecular-glue mechanism.
